key_insight: A DSL-guided multi-agent LLM system can improve inverse materials design by grounding natural-language rules in symbolic predicates and statistical evidence.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical route to discover candidate perovskite oxides for targeted properties without requiring large task-specific training datasets.
method: Translate design rules from natural language into chemistry DSL predicates.
Use accumulated materials data to test, validate, and refine rules during the design loop.
Apply the ORCHESTRA multi-agent framework to inverse design of double perovskite oxides.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that symbolic predicates helped identify unsupported rules, validate new rules, and improve the rule store over iterative design cycles, with better performance than natural-language-only guidance on challenging targets.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on the quality of the predefined DSL and available materials data, so weak symbolic coverage could limit generalization.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
